stimuli.title: Deepa, Esha, Kiran, Charu, Ovi, Hema, Pia, Sana attend interviews, one per slot, on 7 and 21 March, April, May and June. Slots run in chronological order.

stimuli.title: Aditi, Farah, Pia, Sana, Hema, Bina, Kiran, Jaya occupy eight flats on floors 1 (bottom) to 4 (top). Each floor has Flat A to the west of Flat B. Each flat has one resident. For ordering only, count Floor 1 A, Floor 1 B, Floor 2 A, Floor 2 B, and so on.

Use all the following clues:
• Bina occupies floor 1, flat B.
• Sana and Jaya live on the same floor.
• Sana lives above Kiran.
• Farah and Sana occupy flats with the same letter on different floors.

• The floor numbers of Aditi and Pia differ by 3.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some deposits are files. All files are loans. No loans is a coins.
Conclusions:
I. Some deposits are loans.
II. Some files are coins.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few deposits are files. Some files are loans. All loans are coins.
Conclusions:
I. All deposits are coins.
II. No files is a coins.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: No deposits is a files. Some files are loans. All loans are coins.
Conclusions:
I. All deposits are coins.
II. Some coins are files.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few deposits are files. All files are loans. No loans is a coins.
Conclusions:
I. Some deposits are not files.
II. No files is a coins.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: T < U = P > Q > R.
Conclusions: I. P ≤ T   II. U < Q.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
banking rural secure = su lu ni
banking savings access = ni mi pa
rural savings credit = to mi lu
secure access credit = to pa su
banking rural credit = to ni lu
What is the code for “access”?
questions.explanation: Answer: pa. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: banking = ni, rural = lu, secure = su, savings = mi, access = pa, credit = to.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 113 km west, turns right and walks 228 km, then turns right and walks 18 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 247. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 95 km along the initial direction and 228 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(95² + 228²) = 247 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 92 km north, turns right and walks 180 km, then turns right and walks 17 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 195. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 75 km along the initial direction and 180 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(75² + 180²) = 195 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 32 km south, turns right and walks 30 km, then turns right and walks 16 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 34. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 16 km along the initial direction and 30 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(16² + 30²) = 34 km.

questions.stem: D is the mother of H. G is the daughter of H. B is the father of H. How is G related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. B is a parent of H, and G is H’s daughter. Hence G is B’s grandchild.

questions.stem: E is the brother of F. F is the mother of H. G is the father of E and F. How is E related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. E is the brother of H’s mother F. Therefore E is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: B is the only daughter of A. A is the father of B. D is the son of B. C is the sister of A. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. A is the father of B, and B is D’s mother. Thus A is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 64 candidates, a candidate is 17th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 45. New front rank = 17+3 = 20. Back rank = 64 − 20 + 1 = 45.

questions.stem: In a queue of 52 candidates, a candidate is 8th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 41. New front rank = 8+4 = 12. Back rank = 52 − 12 + 1 = 41.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2500 each. One earns 25% profit and the other incurs 10% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 4777.78. Recover each cost separately: 2500×100/125 + 2500×100/90. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 34 and 51 hours. An outlet empties it in 68 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank. (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 29.14. Net rate = 1/34 + 1/51 − 1/68 = 7/204 tank/hour. Required time = 29.14 hours.

questions.stem: A boat covers 78 km in still water in 6 hours. If the stream flows at 3 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 3 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30. Still-water speed = 13 km/h. Upstream speed = 13 − 3. Distance = speed × 3.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 9:6. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 4 months. A receives ₹248400 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 303600. Profit ratio is 108:24. Each ratio unit = ₹2300. Total = 132 × 2300.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹16000 earns ₹9600 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 23040. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 20%. Compound amount = 16000 × (1 + 20/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 90 litres of pure milk. 18 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 57.6. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 90 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 29 people is 51 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 81. New total minus old total = (29+1)×(51+1) − 29×51 = 81.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 20 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 60. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+20)/(x+20) = 3/2 gives x = 20. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 160 m train moving at 68.4 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 14.4 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 10.67. Relative speed = (68.4 − 14.4) ×5/18 = 15 m/s. Time = 160/15.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 50%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹1500. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 33.33. New quantity / old quantity = 100/150. Reduction percentage = 50/150 ×100.
